item.title: Fast GHZ encoding with 1-o(1) fidelity
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Proves (1-o(1))-fidelity N-qubit GHZ state encoding in time O(log N/N) using all-to-all 2-local Hamiltonians, saturating theoretical lower bound Ω(log N/N).

Grade 0.366 · 1.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “quantum machine learning models built from interference and oracle algorithms,…” · Laura Shou, T. C. Mooney, Twesh Upadhyaya, Alexey V. Gorshkov

Figure

Husimi distribution on the Dicke sphere showing the three-step packet separation sequence: deeper initial TAT squeezing, shorter controlled X rotation, and partial reverse TAT squeezing past y = ± 1/3.

Asks

How fast can high-fidelity GHZ encoding be performed using all-to-all interacting Hamiltonians?

Before

was O((log N)^2/N) with unproven non-vanishing infidelity (Yin 2025)

But

All-to-all 2-local Hamiltonians with bounded 2-qubit interactions; asymptotic large N limit.

Tools

two-axis twisting (TAT) · controlled spin rotation · quantum signal processing (QSP) · continuum limit evolution

Abstract

We prove that (1-o(1))-fidelity N-qubit Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) encoding can be performed in time O(logN/N) using all-to-all 2-local Hamiltonians with bounded 2-qubit interaction terms. This saturates the theoretical lower bound Ω(logN/N), and by rescaling, also saturates the lower bound on signaling time for Hamiltonians with power-law interaction strengths 1/r^γ, γ<d in dimension d. The protocol uses spin-squeezing dynamics combined with quantum signal processing.

item.title: Exploiting overcompleteness of Platonic-solid POVMs for shadow estimation
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Estimation variance for molecular Hamiltonians does not scale monotonically with Platonic solid POVM complexity (4 to 20 effects); joint optimization of POVM orientation and weights using an MPS classical proxy state outperforms standard Pauli shadow measurements when bond dimension is sufficiently high.

Grade 0.353 · 1.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum Algorithm for Linear Systems of Equations” · Dario Melegari, Stefano Mangini, Keijo Korhonen, Hetta Vappula, Daniel Cavalcanti

Figure

RMSE versus k-LO dual locality parameter k for a 16-qubit NH3 Hamiltonian across MPS proxy bond dimensions chi = 1, 5, and 10. Performance of optimized Platonic POVMs improves over randomized Pauli baselines as the classical proxy bond dimension increases.

Asks

Can the overcompleteness and symmetry of Platonic-solid POVMs combined with locally optimal dual frames improve shadow estimation variance for molecular Hamiltonians?

Before

Standard randomized Pauli measurement shadow tomography and locally-biased classical shadows (LBCS).

But

Numerical simulations on molecular Hamiltonians up to 16 qubits; relies on MPS proxy approximations with adequate bond dimension; tested primarily with 1-LO dual optimization during parameter search.

Tools

Platonic solid POVMs (4, 6, 8, 12, 20 effects) · k-locally optimal (k-LO) dual frames · Matrix Product State (MPS) proxy optimization · KaHyPar hypergraph partitioning

Abstract

Accurately estimating expectation values of observables from a finite number of measurement shots is a central challenge in quantum information science. Informationally overcomplete measurements provide a route to reduce estimation variance through optimized classical post-processing. However, the interplay between measurement geometry and dual-frame construction remains largely unexplored. In this work, we study Platonic solid POVMs ---highly symmetric, overcomplete single-qubit measurements whose effects correspond to the vertices of the five Platonic solids on the Bloch sphere--- for the estimation of molecular Hamiltonians. Using k-locally optimal dual frames, we show that the geometry of the POVM can have a non-trivial and non-monotonic effect on the estimation variance. We further propose a joint optimization of the POVM orientation and effect weights using a classical proxy state, either a product state or a Matrix Product State (MPS) approximation. We demonstrate that optimized Platonic solid POVMs can outperform standard randomized Pauli measurements, provided the MPS bond dimension is sufficient to faithfully represent the target state. These results reveal a trade-off between classical preprocessing and estimation accuracy, suggesting a practical route to improved observable estimation on near-term quantum hardware.

item.title: Factorized Boolean representations for efficient quantum synthesis
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Extracting shared factors from containment and complementary-polarity relations in Boolean expressions reduces the maximum control count and qubit count of reversible circuits before mapping, never increasing cost measures at the representation level.

Grade 0.346 · 1.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “interpretable quantum machine learning with logic-gate or clause-based classifi…” · Mehul Shah, Robert Fiszer, Marek Perkowski

Asks

Can exploiting algebraic structure beyond classical logic minimization reduce the quantum synthesis cost of Boolean specifications?

Before

Logic minimization followed by standard mapping to reversible circuits.

But

Requires uncomputing auxiliary lines during translation to executable circuits, which offsets part of representation-level gains.

Tools

Factorized Boolean representations · Auxiliary line uncomputation · Quantum circuit synthesis

Abstract

Quantum algorithms promise advantages beyond classical reach, but running them on error-corrected hardware requires translating Boolean specifications into reversible circuits, and the resources that translation demands determine what is executable. Established methods minimize a Boolean expression and map it to a circuit, assuming the minimized form is best. Here we show that minimized expressions retain algebraic structure minimization cannot reach, arising from containment and complementary-polarity relationships among their terms, and that extracting it yields circuits cheaper to execute despite having more operations. The decisive quantity is not a circuit's operation count but the control count of its widest operation, a superlinear cost; extracting shared factors trades a few wide operations for many narrow ones and reduces qubit count. Across benchmarks and oracles from quantum search and factoring algorithms, at the representation level the transformation never increases either cost measure, a guarantee from its construction. Translation to an executable circuit returns part of that advantage, since auxiliary lines must be uncomputed, yet the factorized circuit still left a leading circuit-level optimizer reaching lower final counts, and faster, than unaided. The representation of a computation is therefore itself a resource, optimizable before compilation and distinct from both logic minimization and circuit-level optimization.

item.title: Optimal Gaussian networks for private distributed quantum sensing
item.description:
Worth a look

Grade 0.346 · 1.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum Machine Learning in Feature Hilbert Spaces” · Hanbom Yoo, Byeongyun Yang, Hyunwoo Yoo, Seongjin Hong

Abstract

Private distributed quantum sensing aims to estimate an authorized collective parameter while preventing independent estimation of individual local parameters. Here, we analytically characterize Gaussian quantum networks satisfying this perfect local privacy condition. Using a graph representation of the Gaussian pairing matrix, we show that two-mode squeezed vacuum states constitute the essential building blocks of privacy-preserving Gaussian states. We then analytically derive the optimal sensitivity under perfect local privacy and determine a Gaussian probe that achieves Heisenberg scaling with respect to both the photon number and the number of sensing modes. Using local homodyne measurements and maximum-likelihood estimation, we numerically verify quantum-enhanced sensitivity beyond the shot-noise limit while preserving perfect local privacy. We further show that the local-privacy condition is preserved under arbitrary phase-independent quantum channels, including optical loss. Our results provide a general framework for constructing and optimizing privacy-preserving continuous-variable quantum sensing networks.
